concerns.text: FR-004 mandates a 'blind evaluation' recruitment pipeline to collect ratings from verified experts (ORCID, ≥5 years exp). Tasks T033-T034 only implement loading existing CSV ratings and calculating IRR. There is no task to implement the recruitment logic, blinding mechanism, or data collection interface required to generate the ratings specified in FR-004.

The spec's Edge Cases section requires a fallback behavior if the embedding model fails due to memory constraints (switch to a smaller model). Task T008 only mandates failing 'loudly' on data fetch errors. No task exists to implement the model-fallback logic or the specific logging required for this edge case.

The plan summary describes generating 'pattern-guided vs. random-pattern vs. baseline' proposals (three groups). However, spec FR-003 and tasks T025-T027 strictly define a two-group comparison (pattern-guided vs. baseline). The 'random-pattern' arm promised in the plan has no corresponding task, creating a scope mismatch where the plan element is unimplemented.

SC-004 defines the validity metric as 'downstream expert contextual alignment scores'. Task T023 enforces a retrieval threshold (≥0.6) but does not include a task to correlate or verify that this threshold predicts the downstream expert scores, leaving the validity claim unverified by implementation.

Task T024 implements 'pattern mapping validation' on a hold-out set. The spec FR-002 and SC-004 define validation solely via downstream expert ratings. This task appears to measure a retrieval metric (cosine similarity) rather than the required outcome, creating a potential misalignment of success criteria that needs clarification or removal.
